policy: Exact AST baseline of forbidden-direction imports. A new edge, a grown edge count, a stale entry or a missing reason fails lint via scripts/check_layer_directions.py. Removing an edge requires a reviewed slice with characterization tests; the allowlist is intentionally not auto-fixable.

decisions.infrastructure>application: FORBIDDEN. The application facade owns adapters, not the reverse. A contract belongs to its consumer; infrastructure may not reach into application. Historical edges are inventoried here, not approved as a design.
decisions.ui>presentation: FORBIDDEN. Presentation is the composition root and may mount UI leaf widgets; a leaf widget must not reach back into the shell.
decisions.ui>infrastructure: FORBIDDEN, consistent with the existing presentation->infrastructure ratchet (#307): UI layers go through the application facade, not directly to adapters.
decisions.presentation>ui: ALLOWED. presentation/main_window.py composes ui.strain_window; the composition root may depend on leaf widgets.
decisions.application>infrastructure: ALLOWED. The application facade depends on its adapters (136 existing imports); this is the direction the architecture intends.
decisions.infrastructure>domain: ALLOWED. Adapters use domain contracts and value objects (68 existing imports).
decisions.ui>domain: ALLOWED. Leaf widgets use domain value objects (9 existing imports).
decisions.contract_ownership: application/preferences_contract.py remains in application. It is NOT moved to domain/ports.py in this slice: the consumer (application) owns the contract, and no argument for a domain-side port has been agreed.
decisions.constructor: NOT DECIDED in #419: constructor is a legacy layer (its 14 infrastructure, 14 presentation and 1 domain imports from the 2026-11-02 inventory are out of this slice). It gets its own ownership decision before any ratchet; gating it now would freeze an unagreed boundary.

entries.reason: The DIMSE adapter reads the consumer-owned, read-only transport_policy. Reversing this edge needs an application-side port decision; no mechanical move of the policy.
Measurement persistence reuses an application dataclass as its storage DTO. The DTO stays with its consumer until a storage-owned schema is designed and characterized.
The Orthanc adapter reads the same consumer-owned transport_policy as the DIMSE adapter; one contract, two adapters, no new edge.

The factory wires query/retrieve service constructors; the type-only and lazy imports avoid a runtime cycle but still point the wrong way. Splitting it requires characterization tests for client construction.
Server settings storage reads the consumer-owned transport_policy. This is the same historical edge as the two clients, not a new dependency.

Three names are imported from the application-owned preferences_contract (display scale). The contract stays in application: its consumer owns it, and moving it to domain/ports.py without an owner argument is explicitly out of scope.
The persistent preferences adapter reads the same application-owned preferences_contract. Same ownership decision as ui_scale.py; no mechanical move to domain/ports.py.
Leaf widget imports infrastructure.i18n for tr(); translation is currently a leaf-level utility. A shared i18n owner must be agreed before this edge is removed.
Leaf widget imports infrastructure.i18n and the shared safe_diagnostics helper. Both are cross-cutting utilities whose owner is not yet agreed.
Control panel imports infrastructure.i18n for tr(). Same shared-i18n ownership decision as the other widgets.
STE overview screen imports infrastructure.i18n for tr(). Same shared-i18n ownership decision.
Strain curves view imports infrastructure.i18n for tr(). Same shared-i18n ownership decision.
Strain helpers import infrastructure.i18n for tr(). Same shared-i18n ownership decision.

Strain window imports infrastructure.i18n and safe_diagnostics at module level and infrastructure.profile lazily twice (heavy import kept out of startup). Removing these needs a characterized startup/performance slice.
Summary table imports infrastructure.i18n for tr(). Same shared-i18n ownership decision.

The cine leaf widget imports three presentation helpers (phase strip, segment labels, speckle overlay). They are UI-pure and should move down, but moving code is a separate slice with characterization tests, not part of this gate.
The control panel reads presentation.ui_metrics formatting helpers. Historical reverse edge; a ui-owned formatting module needs its own slice.
The strain window imports presentation.segment_labels. Historical reverse edge; blocked on the same helper migration as cine_panel.py.
The summary table reads presentation.ui_metrics. Historical reverse edge; same migration as control_panel.py.
